Documentation → Tools & Studio → API Catalog

API Catalog — the versions of an API someone publishes

Register an API a team or vendor publishes, one version per release of it, from its OpenAPI document or typed in; pin a connection to a published version and app steps and scripts call its endpoints by id, and only those.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.script_library
📍 WhereAdministrator → Studio → Python Studio → API Catalog (URL /studio/?pane=apis; an API is /studio/apis/<id>, a version /studio/apis/<id>/v/<version>)
On this page
  • What is it?
  • What does it do?
  • Safeguards
  • Permissions
  • How to use
  • Troubleshooting
  • "… is not an endpoint of API … (connection …)"
  • "endpoint … is not in API …"
  • "connection … is not pinned to an API Catalog version, so it has no endpoint …"

  • "neither JSON nor YAML" / "not an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 document"
  • "… is published: a published version never changes"

What is it?#

When a team (or a vendor) publishes an API you want to use, the API Catalog keeps it with one entry per version of it — inventory 1.0, inventory 1.1, inventory 2.0 — and the list of endpoints each version has. A connection pinned to a version then calls exactly that version's endpoints, by name, from app steps and scripts.

What does it do?#

  • Versions with a lifecycle. A draft is edited freely. Publish freezes it for good: its endpoints never change and it is never deleted, so a connection pinned to it means the same endpoints tomorrow. Deprecate marks a version people should move off; it keeps working. Changes go into a new version, which can start from an earlier one.
  • Endpoints from a document or by hand. Import an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 document (JSON or YAML, uploaded or pasted, up to 8 MiB), type the endpoints in (id, method, path with {name} for a path parameter, summary, query parameters, body), or import first and correct by hand.
  • Compare two versions: endpoints removed (calls to them break), changed (method, path, parameters or body) and added.
  • Endpoints (JSON) downloads a version's list in the shape the editor saves, to paste into another version or another SATOM.
  • Pinned connections (HTTP connection page → API version):
  • the Call an API app step offers the version's endpoints in an Endpoint picker; the method and path come from the endpoint and Path parameters ({"id": "{{ form.id }}"}) fill its {name} parts;
  • scripts call endpoints by id:
from satom_script import connection, result

inv = connection("inventory")
host = inv.op("getHost", {"id": 7}).json()
hosts = inv.op("listHosts", params={"limit": 50}).json()
result({"version": inv.catalog()["version"], "endpoints": len(inv.operations())})
  • the script editor's Connections card lists the endpoints of every declared, pinned connection with the line to paste.

Safeguards#

  • Only the version's endpoints. On a pinned connection, a request that is not an endpoint of the version — by id, or a method and path it does not list — is a problem that blocks publishing the app, and is refused before the network when a step or a script sends it. A connection without a version keeps the old behaviour: any path under its base URL.
  • A path parameter is one segment. Each value is percent-encoded, and an encoded / or .. is refused, so a value can never reach another endpoint.
  • A write is a write. An endpoint whose method is POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE counts as a write: a rehearsal (a test run that does not write) never sends it.
  • Nothing is downloaded. Only $ref references inside the document are followed.
  • Moving a connection to another version names the app steps that call an endpoint the new version lacks, and saves only after you confirm.
  • An API with connections pinned to it cannot be deleted; a published version cannot be deleted at all.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Create APIs and versions, import, edit drafts, publish, deprecate; pin a connection studio.script_library

How to use#

  1. Administrator → Studio → Python Studio → API Catalog → New API: a name and an id. On the API page, add the owner and a link to its documentation.
  2. New version → Create draft (empty, or starting from an earlier version).
  3. On the draft, Import the OpenAPI document and/or Add endpoint; Save draft.
  4. Publish.
  5. On an HTTP connection, choose the version under API version and Save. The connection's base URL should end with the version's base path (the page says which).
  6. In an app's Call an API step, pick the endpoint; in a script, declare the connection and call connection("<id>").op("<endpoint id>", {...}).

Troubleshooting#

"… is not an endpoint of API … (connection …)"#

The connection is pinned to a version that does not list that method and path. Pick the endpoint from the picker (app step) or call it by id (script); if the API really has it, add it to a new version and move the connection to that version.

"endpoint … is not in API …"#

The id does not exist in the pinned version — usually after the connection moved to another version. Compare the two versions on the API page to see what was renamed or removed.

"connection … is not pinned to an API Catalog version, so it has no endpoint …"#

An endpoint id only means something on a pinned connection. Pin the connection to a version, or type the method and path instead.

"endpoint … needs path parameter(s) …"#

Give a value for every {name} of the endpoint's path: Path parameters in the app step, the second argument of .op() in a script.

"neither JSON nor YAML" / "not an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 document"#

The file is not an API description, or it is another format. Export the OpenAPI (or Swagger) document from the API itself, or type the endpoints in.

"… is published: a published version never changes"#

Create a new version from it on the API page, change that one and publish it.

#api catalog#openapi#swagger#version#endpoint#operation#operationId#connection#satom_script.connection#op#studio#apps#deprecate#compare
